title: Network Intrusion Detection
mentorBio: Principal Engineer with 12 years in network security and cyber operations. Specialises in intrusion detection systems and adversarial traffic analysis. Led development of DSTA's network anomaly detection framework.
discipline: Computer Science / Information Security / Electrical Engineering
description: Interns will develop and evaluate AI-driven intrusion detection systems (IDS) for military-grade networks. Scope covers anomaly detection modelling, adversarial traffic simulation, and alert triage pipeline design. Learning outcomes include understanding of network threat landscapes and real-time detection architectures. Expected deliverables include a working proof-of-concept IDS with evaluation results against real-world attack datasets.

title: Defence Simulation Modelling
mentorBio: Senior Research Scientist with 9 years in defence operations modelling and simulation. Specialises in discrete-event and agent-based simulation for complex defence planning scenarios.
description: Interns will build and refine discrete-event and agent-based simulation models for defence operational planning scenarios. Scope covers scenario design, performance metric definition, and sensitivity analysis. Learning outcomes include simulation methodologies and their application to complex defence environments. Deliverables include functional simulation modules and a comparative analysis report benchmarking multiple scenario outcomes.

title: Satellite Communications R&D
mentorBio: Principal Engineer with 13 years in satellite and military communications systems. Specialises in waveform design, link budget optimisation, and communication protocols for contested environments.
description: Interns will investigate novel waveform designs and link budget optimisation techniques for next-generation military satellite communications. Scope includes simulation of satellite channel models, signal degradation analysis under contested environments, and protocol evaluation. Deliverables include simulation results, a comparative waveform analysis, and documented recommendations for SATCOM system improvements.

title: Computer Vision for Surveillance
mentorBio: Senior Engineer with 8 years in computer vision and multi-modal perception for defence applications. Specialises in object detection and multi-object tracking under challenging environmental conditions including low-light and occlusion.
description: Interns will develop and benchmark computer vision models for real-time surveillance applications including object detection, multi-object tracking, and scene understanding. Scope includes dataset curation, model training under varied environmental conditions (low-light, occlusion, camouflage), and performance benchmarking. Deliverables include trained model weights, evaluation reports, and a live inference demonstration.

title: Embedded Systems for UAV Control
mentorBio: Senior Engineer with 7 years in embedded systems and UAV control software development. Specialises in real-time operating systems, hardware abstraction layers, and safety-critical software for unmanned platforms.
discipline: Electrical Engineering / Computer Engineering / Mechanical Engineering
description: Interns will design and validate embedded software modules for UAV flight control and payload management systems. Scope covers real-time task scheduling, hardware abstraction layer development, and fail-safe mechanism design. Learning outcomes include embedded systems design principles and safety-critical software development. Deliverables include documented embedded modules and hardware-in-the-loop test results.

title: Logistics Optimisation with AI
mentorBio: Senior Engineer with 10 years in logistics optimisation and AI applications for defence. Specialises in operations research, supply chain modelling, and AI-driven resource allocation under uncertainty.
discipline: Computer Science / Business Analytics / Industrial & Systems Engineering
description: Interns will apply AI and operations research methods to optimise defence logistics networks, covering inventory management, route planning, and resource allocation under uncertainty. Scope includes model development, scenario testing, and integration with existing logistics data pipelines. Deliverables include optimisation models, simulation outputs, and an actionable recommendations report.

title: Cybersecurity Threat Analysis
mentorBio: Senior Research Scientist with 12 years in applied AI and defence analytics. Specialises in machine learning for threat detection and large-scale data fusion. Has led multiple DSTA research programmes in cyber defence.
discipline: Computer Science / Information Security / Computer Engineering
description: Interns will conduct structured threat analysis and develop automated threat intelligence pipelines for defence networks. Scope includes threat modelling using the MITRE ATT&CK framework, malware behavioural analysis, and development of detection rules for SIEM platforms. Learning outcomes include adversarial thinking and practical cyber defence workflows. Deliverables include threat reports, SIEM detection rule sets, and a documented threat modelling framework.

title: AI/ML in Defence Logistics
mentorBio: Senior Research Scientist with 9 years in machine learning and predictive analytics for defence logistics. Specialises in demand forecasting, predictive maintenance, and end-to-end ML pipeline development in operational settings.
discipline: Computer Science / Business Analytics / Industrial & Systems Engineering
description: Interns will develop machine learning models to improve predictive maintenance scheduling and inventory demand forecasting for defence assets. Scope includes data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training and evaluation, and integration with logistics management dashboards. Learning outcomes cover end-to-end ML pipeline development in an operational setting. Deliverables include trained models, evaluation benchmarks, and deployment-ready documentation.

title: Signal Processing R&D
mentorBio: Principal Engineer with 15 years in radar signal processing and electronic warfare systems. Specialises in adaptive filtering, target detection under clutter, and signal classification for defence applications.
description: Interns will research and prototype signal processing algorithms for radar and electronic warfare applications. Scope covers adaptive filtering, target detection under clutter, and signal classification using ML techniques. Learning outcomes include deep understanding of DSP theory and its real-world defence applications. Deliverables include algorithm implementations in MATLAB and Python, performance benchmarks against synthetic and operational datasets, and a technical research report.

title: Autonomous Systems Prototyping
mentorBio: Lead Engineer with 10 years in autonomous ground and aerial vehicle development. Heads DSTA's Autonomous Systems Lab and specialises in robotics middleware, navigation stack integration, and field system testing.
discipline: Mechanical Engineering / Electrical Engineering / Computer Engineering
description: Interns will contribute to prototyping and integration of autonomous system modules for unmanned ground and aerial vehicles. Scope covers sensor integration, navigation stack development, and obstacle avoidance algorithm implementation. Learning outcomes include hands-on experience with robotics middleware and system integration workflows. Deliverables include functional prototype modules, ROS package documentation, and field test results.

title: Sensor Fusion for ISR Systems
mentorBio: Senior Engineer with 8 years in multi-sensor fusion and ISR system development. Specialises in Kalman filtering, radar-optical data fusion, and multi-target tracking for intelligence and surveillance platforms.
discipline: Electrical Engineering / Computer Engineering / Computer Science
description: Interns will develop and validate multi-sensor fusion algorithms for Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) platforms. Scope includes Kalman and particle filter design, radar-optical data fusion, and multi-target tracking under occlusion. Learning outcomes include mastery of state estimation techniques and multi-modal sensing architectures. Deliverables include fusion algorithm implementations, performance evaluation reports, and integration documentation.

title: Drone Payload Optimisation
mentorBio: Lead Engineer with 11 years in UAV systems engineering and payload integration. Specialises in aerodynamic modelling, structural load analysis, and multi-mission drone configuration for defence platforms.
discipline: Mechanical Engineering / Aerospace Engineering / Electrical Engineering
description: Interns will optimise payload integration and weight distribution strategies for multi-mission UAV platforms. Scope covers aerodynamic modelling, structural load analysis under flight conditions, and payload configuration trade-off studies. Learning outcomes include applying aerospace engineering principles to real UAV design constraints. Deliverables include optimised payload configuration designs, simulation results, and a documented engineering analysis with recommendations.
